How it works

How you get a price from us

Four steps, no sales appointment, and nothing you have to sit through.

  1. You call or send the form. One number, 708-935-4289, and it goes to the company rather than a call center. Texting a photo of the room or the front of the house is the fastest thing you can do.
  2. We come and look at it. Somebody stands in the room, counts the doors and the trim runs, and looks at the condition of what is already on the wall. There is no honest way to price this work off a photograph, and a number given without a visit is a guess made in the contractor’s favor.
  3. You get the number and what sits behind it. What is included, how many coats, what the preparation is, and what happens to the price if the preparation turns out worse than it looks. That last line is the one to compare between quotes.
  4. We book a date and do the work. You know who is coming and roughly how many days it takes. The owner runs the job, so if something changes you hear it from the person responsible for it.

On the day

What it is like having us working in your house

  • You can carry on living there. We work room by room. Furniture moves to the middle and gets covered, floors get protected, and doors stay shut so the dust stays where the work is.
  • You get your house back every evening. Tools and materials get packed up at the end of the day rather than left across your living room for a week.
  • You know who is coming. Our own crew, run by the owner, not a different subcontracted van every morning.
  • The room goes back together. Furniture back where it was, hardware and switch plates back on, floors clear. Putting the room back is part of the job, not a favor.
  • If you hate it, say so on day one. Colors look different on a wall than they do on a chip. Tell us early and it is a small conversation. Tell us at the end and it is a repaint.

Why people call us

What a local owner gives you that a franchise branch cannot

  • The person who quotes it is the person running it. Mike Walsh owns the company. He walks the job, prices it, and stays on it while our crew works. Nothing gets promised at your kitchen table by a salesman on commission and then forgotten by the start date.
  • We can finish the whole job. Painting, carpentry, tile, flooring, subfloors, concrete and faux finishes. When a bathroom repaint turns out to be a soft subfloor, it does not turn into a month of hunting for a second contractor.
  • We are actually from here. The shop is in Bridgeview, about where the city stops and the southwest suburbs start. We work the south side and the towns south and southwest of it. Not the whole metro, and not a territory map drawn up in another state.
  • If something is wrong there is one person to tell. One number, one owner, no branch manager to be escalated to. That is the whole of it.

Straight answers

License, insurance and guarantee: the honest version

Most contractor websites carry a row of badges with nothing behind any of them. Here is what we can and cannot show you, and what the word "licensed" actually means for a painter in Illinois.

  • InsuranceTo supply
  • Local registrationTo supply
  • Workmanship guaranteeTo supply
  • Lead-safe certificationTo supply

Why these say "to supply"

Because the real values have not been handed over yet, and putting a plausible looking number in an empty box is how a website starts lying on a business owner's behalf. They will appear here exactly as they are, and not before.

Worth knowing while you compare quotes: Illinois does not license painters or general contractors at state level. The state licenses roofing contractors under the Illinois Roofing Industry Licensing Act, and IDFPR does not list painter, painting contractor, general contractor or remodeler as regulated professions. So a "licensed" badge on a painting company's website in this state does not mean what most people assume it means. Insurance is the thing that actually protects you, and it is worth asking every contractor to show you the certificate.

Sources: IDFPR list of regulated professions, 225 ILCS 335.

Questions

The things people ask us before they call

Do you cover my town?

Chicago and the south and southwest suburbs. The shop is in Bridgeview, so the close ring is Oak Lawn, Burbank, Evergreen Park, Palos Hills, Palos Heights, Hickory Hills, Chicago Ridge, Worth, Justice and Summit, and we go out as far as Orland Park, Tinley Park, Mokena, Frankfort and Lemont. On the city side it is the south and southwest sides. There is a page for every town we cover, and if yours is not on it, call and ask rather than assume.

How much is this going to cost?

That depends on things nobody can see in a photograph, which is why there are no prices on this site. On an interior it comes down to the condition of what is already on the wall and how much trim there is. Send us photos and we will tell you what to expect, then we come and look and you get a real number.

Do you do small jobs?

Yes. One room, one wall, one ceiling, a patch, a door. Close to the shop a small repair is worth a trip on its own. Further out it is worth asking, and you will get a straight answer about whether the drive makes sense rather than a quiet no.

Do you do more than painting?

Yes, and that is unusual around here. Alongside interior and exterior painting we do carpentry, tile, flooring, subfloor repair, concrete, faux finishes and general remodeling. The point is not a longer list. It is that your job does not stop dead when it turns out to need more than paint.

Who will actually be in my house?

Our own crew, run by the owner. Mike Walsh owns the company, walks and prices the job himself, and stays on it while it runs. There is no branch office and no salesperson on commission standing between you and the people doing the painting.

Are you insured?

Ask on the phone and you will get a straight answer. Insurance and any local registration details go on this website the moment the paperwork is handed over, and not a day before. Nothing is claimed here that has not been produced.

Can I read your reviews?

Not yet. This business has run on word of mouth and a van, and no reviews have been collected. Rather than fill the page with something invented, the space is left empty until there are real ones to put in it.
